tells.1: none (slightly clunky, repetitive phrasing like 'blood work done' twice reads authentically human)
tells.2: em-dash-heavy marketing cadence and the tacked-on value pitch 'a practical way to get a fuller picture... make the most of their yearly checkup'
tells.3: over-trimmed, uniformly short declarative sentences that feel mechanically pared down
tells.4: mild tidy parallel structure ('which helps guide care as your dog ages'), otherwise minimal

reason: Version 1 has the natural awkwardness of a real clinic writer, but Version 4 keeps the human tone, explains the before-symptoms and baseline benefits clearly, and avoids the salesy em-dash padding of Version 2 and the clipped stiffness of Version 3.
